FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 August 1979, after the draft finalized by the Cotton and Cotton Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council.

0.2 Chafer fabric is awoven fabric which is generally coated with unvulcaThis mzed rubber and laid around the bead of a tyre before curing. fabric is used to maintain an abrasion resistant layer in contact with the rim of the wheel on which the tyre is mounted. 0.3 To familiarize the industry with International System ( SI Units ) the basic SI Units as well as the recommended SI use in the textile industry are given in Appendix C. 0.3.1 Standards of SI Units. of Weights and Measures Act, of Units Units for use

1976 also stipulates

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, with expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance IS : 2-1960*.' The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of cotton chafer fabrics used in the manufacture of automobile tyres, other than motor-cycle and scooter tyres.
1.2 This standard also gives the constructional particulars popular varieties of cotton chafer fabrics for information only.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

IS : 9230 - 1979 2. MANUFACTURE 2.1 Yarn - The yarn used in the manufacture of chafer fabrics shall be satisfactory in evenness and shall be reasonably free from neps, spinning and doubling defects.
2.2 Cloth - The cloth shall be evenly and firmly woven in plain weave. The cloth when visuaily examined shall be reasonably free from foreign matter and such defects as knots, lumps and irregularities of twist in yarn. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 The cotton in Table 1. chafer fabrics shall conform to the requirements as given

5. MARKING 5.1 Each roll shall be marked a) Name of the material; or trade-mark, if any; with the following:

b) Name of the manufacturer, initials c) Length and width of roll; and d) Year of manufacture. 5.2 BIS Certification Marking

The product may also be marked with Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

5

IS : 9230 - 1979 6. PACKING 6.1 The rolls shall be tightly wrapped with a layer of polyethylene film and hessian and sewn tightly all over or as agreed to between the buyer If necessary, additional layers of packing materials may and the seller. be used to avoid ingress of moisture in transit.
7. SAMPLING

7.1 For ascertaining

the conformity in respect of length, width, breaking the number of tests and criteria load, mass, ends, picks and thickness, for conformity as given in IS : 3919-1966* shall be followed.

7.2 For ascertaining the conformity in respect of freedom from starch, the number of tests and criteria for conformity as given in IS : 54 3-19697 shall be followed.

APPENDiX ( Clause 3.3 )
METHOD B-l. TEST FOR DETERMINING

B
STARCH CONTENT

SPECIMEN test sample. Shred the Draw from the pieces so

B-l.1 Cut a piece weighing about 10 g from the piece into small bits and mix them thoroughly. shredded a test specimen of about 5 g. B-2. PROCEDURE

B-2.1 Boil the test specimen in about 200 ml of distilled water in a conical flask for about 45 minutes. Cool the contents in the flask. Put a drop of iodine solution on a smaller quantity taken from the flask. B-3. REPORT of blue colour on adding to be free from starch if

B-3.1 Observe whether there is any appearance a drop of iodine solution. Report the material no blue colour is observed.
